notes:
Background: LocaleSentry operates a global outsourced support platform for fintech and e-commerce customers. Primary pain: multilingual scale during regional peaks (EMEA holiday windows + NA flash promotions). Current stack: Zendesk + homegrown router + third-party MT as fallback. Evaluation goal: replace brittle MT + add real-time agent-assist and ticket summarization with locale-aware tone.

Key reqs (from CTPO/ops):
- Latency: 90th pct < 250ms for agent-assist token-level responses during normal load; graceful degradation under spikes (target: degrade to synopsis-only, not full fail).
- Throughput: support bursts up to ~450 concurrent agent sessions across regions, sustained message rate ~6k messages/min during promotions.
- Quality: locale-aware tone controls (formal vs casual per locale), locale-specific routing (EU francophone -> FR hub), and maintain audit trail for each generated output.
- Integrations: Zendesk tool-calls (create/update ticket, pull customer context), Salesforce sync for case metadata, SSO via SAML, KMS for key management.
- Compliance: SOC2 required, data residency for EU customers, retention controls for PII.

POC details & feedback:
- Scope: two scenarios: (1) agent-assist augmented responses + live tone picker; (2) ticket summarization pipeline that creates TL;DR + suggested tags and escalation reasons.
- Week 1: ingestion/connectors, routing rules, caching configs.
- Week 2: model variants tested (Llama-variant quantized vs open-sft), fallback chaining (fast smaller model -> high-quality synth) implemented. Customer noted: "we need deterministic fallback ordering, can't have surprises mid-session."
- Week 3: stress test with synthetic traffic simulating 3x peak; Redwood logging captured token-level cost; initial optimizations cut per-token cost by estimated 28%.

Open security items:
- LocaleSentry infosec asked for encryption at rest proof, KMS integration plan, and SOC2 artifact timeline. Drive: security doc link above.
- Legal pushing hard on data residency contract clause for EU customers; clause needs to be explicit about model caching and KV storage.

Commercial notes:
- Customer prefers Dedicated pools for predictable cost during spikes but wants option to burst to hosted for overflow.
- Negotiation points: SLA for P90 latency, retention window defaults, and egress cost caps.

Quotes / snippets:
- CTO: "Tone and trust are our two blockers — translations must respect regional phrasing and not sound 'AI-generic'."
- Head of Ops: "If we can get predictable cost and a clean security story, we can convert three enterprise customers currently on our pipeline."

Next actions (short):
- Send finalized security questionnaire and SOC2 roadmap by 2024-11-22.
- Draft dedicated + overflow pricing scenario and share with procurement.
- Arrange 1-hour legal sync to resolve residency contract language (target week of 2024-11-25).
